predecessors.note: Infobox 'Predecessor: Pratihara dynasty; Tomara dynasty'. The Pratihara dossier records the loss of Rajasthan at 960.

land.text: Ajmer and the Chahamana kingdom, which 'Muhammad of Ghor appointed Prithviraja's son Govindaraja IV as a vassal' to hold in 1192; Hariraja was defeated by the Ghurids in 1194
Ranthambore: 'Govindaraja was granted the fief of Ranthambore by the Ghurids' and 'established a new branch of the dynasty'

capitals.name: Ajayameru (Ajmer)
capitals.note: Ajayaraja II moved the capital to Ajmer in the early 12th century (the page gives no year; his reign begins 1110). Prithviraj III ruled 'with his capital at Ajmer' (Prithviraj page); the Delhi of the legends was not his capital.

rulers.name: Simha-raja
rulers.note: R. B. Singh's list; 'assumed the title Maharajadhiraja'.

rulers.name: Vigraha-raja II
rulers.note: His 973 inscription is the dynasty earliest extant.

rulers.name: Viryarama
rulers.note: A few months; killed by Bhoja (Bhoja page).

rulers.name: Someshvara
rulers.note: Table: 1169-1178; Prithviraja III is listed from 1177.

rulers.name: Prithviraja III (Rai Pithora)
rulers.note: 'Ascending the throne as a minor in 1177 CE' (Prithviraj page); killed or executed after Tarain in 1192.

rulers.name: Govinda-raja IV
rulers.title: Ghurid vassal at Ajmer
rulers.note: Dethroned in 1192 by Hariraja; granted Ranthambore.

correction.text: Shakambhari (modern Sambhar) and the Ajmer country, the Chahamana homeland of Sapadalaksha

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 944-979: Cliopatria's row begins in 980. The page makes Simharaja (944-971) 'assume the title Maharajadhiraja' and 'assert independence' of the Gurjara-Pratiharas (undated in the text; 944 is the start of his reign in R. B. Singh's table) and gives the dynasty's 'earliest extant inscription (973 CE)' under Vigraharaja II. The infobox 'Established: 551' dates the legendary house, not the state. Drawn as the homeland at Shakambhari and Ajmer; the page gives no area.

union.text: the Shakambhari-Ajmer cells that Cliopatria draws as Paramara in 980-1055 and as Chauhan from 1056

correction.text: the Rajasthan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape (695 cells) plus the Shakambhari-Ajmer cells that Cliopatria gives to the Paramaras; Punjab and Haryana removed

keyframe_review.note: 242,471 km2 for 980-1027 (no infobox area, so no comparison). Cliopatria's shape holds 695 cells of Rajasthan, 97 of Haryana, 108 of Indian Punjab and 24 of Pakistani Punjab. The Tomara page has the Tomaras 'ruled the Hariyanaka (Haryana) country before the Chahamanas' and Haryana ('the Tomara kingdom stretched to Hansi and Thanesar area') in Tomara hands until Vigraharaja IV took Delhi and Hansi (c. 1151); no page opened gives the Chahamanas Punjab before Prithviraja III. Punjab and Haryana are dropped; the Ajmer-Shakambhari cells that Cliopatria gives to the Paramaras are added (Bhoja held them only 'for a brief period' c. 1040).

union.text: the Shakambhari-Ajmer cells that Cliopatria draws as Paramara in 980-1055 and as Chauhan from 1056

correction.text: the Rajasthan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape (695 cells) plus the Shakambhari-Ajmer cells that Cliopatria gives to the Paramaras; Punjab and Haryana removed

keyframe_review.note: 243,174 km2 for 1028-1055: the 980 shape plus 700 km2; same correction. The Chahamana page: 'The subsequent Chahamana kings faced several Ghaznavid raids' (no year); Bhoja invaded in c. 1040 under Viryarama.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1056 shape within Rajasthan (572 cells); the years are 1056-1150

keyframe_review.note: 149,884 km2 for 1056-1176: 411 cells lost in 1056 (189 in Rajasthan, 81 in Haryana, 108 in Indian Punjab and 28 in Pakistani Punjab, mostly inside Cliopatria's Ghaznavid 1056 shape) and 66 gained (the Paramara cells at Ajmer). Haryana (16 cells here) is removed until the capture of Delhi and Hansi; the Rajasthan shape is kept. Holds 1056-1150; 'Vigraharaja IV greatly expanded the Chahamana territories, and captured Delhi from the Tomaras' (reign 1150-1164; the page's quoted reference has 1151).

union.text: Delhi (Dhillika) and Hansi, Haryana: the Tomara country taken by Vigraharaja IV

correction.text: Rajasthan (Cliopatria's 1056 shape) plus Delhi and Haryana from the Tomaras

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1151-1176: 'His kingdom included parts of the present-day Rajasthan, Haryana, and Delhi' (Vigraharaja IV, 1150-1164); the Tomara page: his brother 'had captured Dhillika (Delhi) and Ashika (Hansi)'. His 1164 Delhi-Shivalik pillar 'claims that he conquered the region between the Himalayas and the Vindhyas', which the page calls an exaggeration. The 1170 Bijolia inscription of Someshvara is the other source of the realm.

union.text: Delhi (Dhillika) and Hansi, Haryana: the Tomara country taken by Vigraharaja IV

correction.text: Rajasthan (Cliopatria's 1056 shape) plus Delhi and Haryana from the Tomaras

keyframe_review.note: 149,240 km2 for 1177-1191: the shape lacks Delhi and Haryana. Prithviraj III, from 1177, 'inherited a kingdom which stretched from Thanesar in the north to Jahazpur (Mewar) in the south' (other authors: 'only stretched till modern day Hissar and Sirhind'); at its height, per R. B. Singh, 'from Sutlej river in the west to the Betwa river in the east'. The corrected shape adds Delhi and Haryana; the Sutlej-to-Betwa claim is not drawn. Delhi is not a capital: 'with his capital at Ajmer'.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1192 shape within Rajasthan; the years are 1192-1194, as a Ghurid vassal kingdom

keyframe_review.note: 149,884 km2 for 1192-1201, the shape of 1056. After the Second Battle of Tarain the Ghurids hold Delhi and Haryana (Cliopatria's Ghurid 1192 shape covers 145 of Haryana's 166 cells); 'The Ghurids then appointed his son Govindaraja IV on the throne of Ajmer as their vassal', Hariraja 'dethroned Govindaraja' in 1192 and was 'defeated by the Ghurids in 1194 CE', which ends the dynasty of Shakambhari; a branch continued at Ranthambore. The Rajasthan part is kept for 1192-1194 as the Ghurid vassal kingdom; Cliopatria's 1195-1201 belongs to the Ghurids and the Ranthambore branch.

region.text: Shakambhari (modern Sambhar) and the Ajmer country, the Chahamana homeland of Sapadalaksha

ledger.note: c. 944: Simharaja makes the Chahamanas independent at Shakambhari. 'Simharaja assumed the title Maharajadhiraja' and 'asserted independence' of the Gurjara-Pratiharas (undated; his reign is 944-971 in the page's table); Vakpatiraja I had 'made an attempt to overthrow the Gurjara-Pratihara suzerainty' in the 10th century. The earliest extant inscription is 973 (Vigraharaja II). The infobox 'Established: 551' is the legendary Vasudeva.

minus.text: Shakambhari (modern Sambhar) and the Ajmer country, the Chahamana homeland of Sapadalaksha

region.text: the Rajasthan part of Cliopatria's 980 shape beyond the Ajmer country

ledger.note: 980 (bridge): the Rajasthan beyond the homeland. Cliopatria's row starts with 695 cells of Rajasthan; the page says only that the dynasty ruled 'parts of present-day Rajasthan and neighbouring areas' and fought the Chaulukyas and Tomaras (undated). The Pratihara dossier records Rajasthan lost to its feudatories in 960. Page silent on the year and the limits.

region.text: the Shakambhari-Ajmer cells that Cliopatria draws as Paramara in 980-1055 and as Chauhan from 1056

ledger.note: c. 1040: Bhoja takes Shakambhari. 'During the reign of Viryarama (r. c. 1040 CE), the Paramara king Bhoja invaded the Chahamana kingdom' and 'probably occupied their capital Shakambhari for a brief period'; the Bhoja page: he 'defeated and killed Viryarama'.

region.text: the Shakambhari-Ajmer cells that Cliopatria draws as Paramara in 980-1055 and as Chauhan from 1056

ledger.note: 1056 (bridge): the Chahamanas are back. 'Chamundaraja restored the Chahamana power, possibly with the help of the Naddula Chahamanas' (reign 1040-1065 on the table; no year). Cliopatria gives the cells to the Chauhan row in 1056.

region.text: the margins of Rajasthan that Cliopatria's 1056 shape drops

ledger.note: 1056 (bridge): the northern and western margins leave the Chahamana shape. Cliopatria drops 189 cells of Rajasthan in 1056 (104 inside its Ghaznavid 1056 shape, 28 inside the Chaulukya 1111 shape). The page records only undated Ghaznavid raids and wars with the Chaulukyas; page silent on the year and the land.
c. 1110: Ajayaraja II moves the capital to Ajmer. 'Ajayaraja II moved the capital there in the early 12th century' (Ajayameru, modern Ajmer); his reign begins in 1110 on the table.

region.text: Delhi (Dhillika) and Hansi, Haryana: the Tomara country taken by Vigraharaja IV

ledger.note: c. 1151: Vigraharaja IV takes Delhi and Hansi from the Tomaras. 'greatly expanded the Chahamana territories, and captured Delhi from the Tomaras'; the quoted reference: 'In 1151 the Tomar Rajput rulers (and original builders) of Delhi were overthrown by Visal Dev'; the Tomara page: 'had captured Dhillika (Delhi) and Ashika (Hansi)' and ends the Tomaras 'c. 1152'. The page gives no year in its narrative.

region.text: Jejakabhukti, the Chandela country, and Mahoba

ledger.note: 1182-83: Prithviraj III raids the Chandelas. 'The 1182-83 CE (1239 VS) Madanpur inscriptions ... claim that he 'laid to waste' Jejakabhukti' and 'Prithviraj sacked Mahoba'; Talbot: 'Prithviraj was not able to annex the Chandela territory'.
1183: the Mahoba campaign ends without annexation (R. B. Singh: 'some part of Chandela territory was annexed by Chahmanas albeit for a short time').

region.text: Tabarhindah (Bathinda) and Tarain (Taraori, near Karnal), the frontier of Haryana and Punjab

ledger.note: 1190-1191: Muhammad of Ghor invades. 'During 1190-1191 CE, Muhammad of Ghor invaded the Chahamana territory, and captured Tabarhindah or Tabar-e-Hind (identified with Bathinda).' The First Battle of Tarain in 1191 was a Chahamana victory: Muhammad 'was injured and forced to retreat'.

region.text: Tarain and the frontier of Haryana and Punjab

ledger.note: 1192: the Second Battle of Tarain ends the contest in a Ghurid victory. 'The battle ended in a decisive victory for the invading Ghurids'; infobox 'Muhammad Ghuri conquers much of northwestern India including Delhi'.

region.text: Delhi (Dhillika) and Hansi, Haryana: the Tomara country taken by Vigraharaja IV

ledger.note: 1192: Delhi and Haryana to the Ghurids. 'Muhammad Ghuri conquers much of northwestern India including Delhi' (Second Tarain infobox); the Tomara page: the Tomaras 'were themselves soon displaced by the Ghurid ruler Muhammad of Ghor in 1192 CE'. Cliopatria's Ghurid 1192 shape covers 145 Haryana cells. [Reviewer sa-03-f, 2026-10-19] Confidence 3 to 2: the cited pages name Delhi, not Haryana (Second Tarain infobox: "conquers much of northwestern India including Delhi").

region.text: Ajmer and the Chahamana kingdom in Rajasthan, Sapadalaksha

ledger.note: 1192: Ajmer becomes Ghurid. 'The Ghurids then appointed his son Govindaraja IV on the throne of Ajmer as their vassal'; the Ghurids 'subjugated the entire Chahamana territory of Siwalikh (Sapadalaksha)'; Hariraja 'dethroned Govindaraja' the same year and 'recaptured a part of his ancestral kingdom' (Prithviraj page). [Reviewer sa-03-f, 2026-10-19] Type loss to vassal_start: Second Tarain page, "The Ghurids then appointed his son Govindaraja IV on the throne of Ajmer as their vassal"; the Chahamana state goes on under Ghurid suzerainty until the 1194 dissolve (Hariraja "was defeated by the Ghurids in 1194 CE"), so the vassal carries the vassal_start too (brief 2.3).

region.text: the last Chahamana kingdom, Ajmer and Rajasthan

ledger.note: 1194: Hariraja is defeated by the Ghurids and the Chahamana dynasty of Shakambhari ends. 'Hariraja was defeated by the Ghurids in 1194 CE', 'bringing the Chahamana dynasty of Shakambhari to an end'; a branch rules Ranthambore. Cliopatria's row ends in 1201.

wars.name: Ghaznavid raids on the Chahamanas
wars.outcome: 'The subsequent Chahamana kings faced several Ghaznavid raids' (no year); 'Ajayaraja II (r. c. 1110-1135 CE) repulsed a Ghaznavid attack'.
wars.note: The page gives the raids only as 11th-century; 1001 is the start of the century, 1135 the end of Ajayaraja II.

wars.name: Bhoja's invasion of Shakambhari

zones.text: the Shakambhari-Ajmer cells that Cliopatria draws as Paramara in 980-1055 and as Chauhan from 1056

wars.outcome: Bhoja invaded in the reign of Viryarama, 'probably occupied their capital Shakambhari for a brief period' and killed Viryarama; Chamundaraja restored the Chahamanas.

wars.name: Chahamana-Tomara wars

zones.text: Delhi (Dhillika) and Hansi, Haryana: the Tomara country taken by Vigraharaja IV

wars.outcome: Arnoraja 'raided the Tomara territory'; Vigraharaja IV captured Delhi and Hansi c. 1151.

wars.name: Prithviraj III-Chandela war (Mahoba)
wars.outcome: Mahoba sacked in 1182-83; no annexation (Talbot), or a short-lived one (R. B. Singh).

wars.name: Chahamana-Chaulukya war of Prithviraja III
wars.outcome: Prithviraj 'invaded Gujarat but could not gain much success and concluded a peace treaty with Chaulukya Bhima II' (before 1187).

wars.name: First Battle of Tarain
wars.outcome: Muhammad of Ghor captured Tabarhindah (Bathinda) in 1190-1191; Prithviraj's army 'decisively defeated the Ghurids' at Tarain in 1191.

wars.name: Second Battle of Tarain
wars.outcome: Decisive Ghurid victory near Tarain; Prithviraj killed or executed; Govindaraja IV installed at Ajmer as a Ghurid vassal.

wars.name: Ghurid conquest of Hariraja
wars.outcome: Hariraja dethroned Govindaraja IV in 1192 and was defeated by Qutb al-Din Aibak, 'in 1194 CE'; the dynasty of Shakambhari ended.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line appears on any page opened. The Chahamana kingdom is described by its inscriptions' claims (Sapadalaksha, Hansi, the Himalayas to the Vindhyas) and by the sites of its battles; the frontier with the Ghurids near Tarain, Hansi and Bathinda changed with each campaign of 1190-1192.

notes:
WIKIDATA. Cliopatria gives Q1068371 to both this row ('Chauhan Dynasty') and 'Han Dynasty' (han-dynasty). They are different states (a north Indian Rajput dynasty and the Chinese Han); the id belongs to only one of them and Wikidata is unreachable, so it is kept here as Cliopatria gives it and the state page link should be checked.
NAME. 'Chauhan Dynasty' is Cliopatria's name; the English Wikipedia article read is 'Chahamanas of Shakambhari' (the 'Chauhan Dynasty' title redirects there, unconfirmed).
Corrections: (1) Cliopatria's 980-1055 shape holds Punjab and Haryana that no page gives the Chahamanas; removed. (2) The shape stops at the Rajasthan border until Vigraharaja IV takes Delhi and Hansi (c. 1151); the corrected 1151 keyframe adds Delhi and Haryana (all of Haryana, because the page puts Prithviraj III's kingdom 'from Thanesar in the north'; other authors say only to Hissar and Sirhind). (3) The Cliopatria row runs to 1201; the page ends the dynasty in 1194 and puts the Ranthambore branch afterwards.
Not settled: the 1056 loss of 189 Rajasthan cells (page silent); the 944 start (R. B. Singh's table, not a dated source); the extent of the Chahamanas in 980-1150 (the page gives no area, no boundary); whether the 'First Battle of Tarain' victory regained Bathinda (the pages are silent). The page does not date Arnoraja's 'Slaughter of Turushkas' near Ajmer or the Ghaznavid defeat by Vigraharaja IV (Khusrau Shah). Counterparts without a dossier: tomara-dynasty (c. 736-c. 1152), chahamanas-of-ranastambhapura (1192 on). Gazetteer names needed: Bathinda (30.21 N 74.95 E), Ranthambore (26.02 N 76.46 E), Sambhar (26.91 N 75.19 E). Pages (4 of 5): Chahamanas of Shakambhari (opened twice), Second Battle of Tarain, Prithviraj Chauhan, Tomara dynasty; the 1040 event is cited from the Chahamana page, with the Bhoja page (opened for the Paramara dossier) in its note.
